paths.description: Requested service host and resulting courtesy/error state; represents the only directly exposed target entry template.
The linked INPS homepage used as the advertised recovery destination and as a representative public content/navigation surface.
The prominent Accedi route, exercised to test the account journey; it resolves to the same courtesy 404.

findings.summary: The requested service host does not expose a usable entry experience.
findings.evidence: HAR records the target document returning HTTP 500, followed by a redirect to an INPS courtesy document returning HTTP 404. Desktop and mobile screenshots show “Pagina non disponibile”; the linked login route also resolves to the same 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a successful service entry route, preserve valid deep links, and return a purposeful recovery page only for genuinely missing URLs.

findings.summary: The cookie notice obscures most content, especially on mobile.
findings.evidence: The 360×800 screenshot shows the fixed cookie panel occupying almost the entire viewport before interaction. DOM evidence reports no dialog, popover, or details primitive.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, semantic consent dialog with focus management and equal accept/reject choices; defer nonessential detail to settings.

findings.summary: The interface does not honor the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot remains fully light; computed color-scheme is “normal” and CSS inspection found zero prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface, text, border, illustration, and browser-chrome colors.

findings.summary: The recovery homepage is slow, unstable, and ships substantial avoidable code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 8.8 s, FCP 3.6 s, TBT 350 ms, CLS 0.111, 3,364 KiB total weight, 546 KiB unused JS and 118 KiB unused CSS. Mobile layout independently observed CLS 0.104 and a 218 ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reserve late content space, defer noncritical scripts/styles, remove unused bundles, and split work into sub-50 ms tasks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on ordinary navigation controls.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found outline-style none and no box shadow on the primary “Pensione e Previdenza” link/button and subsequent navigation links; only skip links had an outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator that is not clipped and remains visible across all links, buttons, menus, and consent controls.

findings.summary: The target response omits baseline browser security headers.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, nosniff, a restrictive CSP including frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy on the entry response and redirects.

findings.summary: Analytics and third-party dependencies load before consent on the initial view.
findings.evidence: HAR/trackers evidence records 33 of 35 requests as third-party relative to the requested host, including Adobe, Helix RUM, Dynatrace/INPS analytics and Azure-hosted chat resources; Lighthouse reports a third-party cookie.
findings.suggestedFix: Load only essential first-party resources before consent, gate analytics/chat, minimize fields and retention, batch telemetry, and document each processor.

findings.summary: The public entry URL emits contradictory failure and indexing signals.
findings.evidence: The target returns 500 then serves a 404 courtesy page with no canonical or meta description and robots “noindex, nofollow”; sitemap.xml itself returns an HTML 404. The title identifies a 404 rather than the requested service.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a 200 response for the real entry page with a unique title, description, canonical, crawlable links, and a valid sitemap; retain noindex only on actual error documents.

findings.summary: The page records runtime/network errors and browser inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found a failed Matomo request and Chrome inspector issues; the HAR also contains document 500/404 responses.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or correct failing telemetry calls, resolve inspector issues, and monitor uncaught exceptions and failed requests in release checks.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports aria-allowed-attr and malformed accessibility-tree failures. On the courtesy page, the visible “Pagina non disponibile” is an h2 with no visible-content h1, while hidden/template headings precede it.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct invalid ARIA, expose one logical h1 for the page, remove hidden duplicate heading structure from the accessibility tree, and validate the final accessibility tree.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior relies on global styling rather than component containment.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout fits without horizontal overflow, but live stylesheet inspection found zero container rules despite a large reused component/navigation system.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable regions and use @container rules so cards, navigation, search, and consent UI adapt to their allocated space.

findings.summary: The public landing experience transfers and executes work disproportionate to its first view.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 3,364 KiB total, 546 KiB unused JS and 118 KiB unused CSS; the DOM contains 1,144 anchors including 156 hash-only links, while analytics, chat, and several undeferred scripts load immediately.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not serialize hidden mega-menu content or load chat/analytics upfront; lazy-render offscreen navigation and conditionally import feature code.
